title: sterculia coccinea var. hamiltonii
intro: Sterculia coccinea var. hamiltonii, commonly known as the Red Stinking Nuts or Red Stinking Corpse Flower, is a plant species native to the tropical regions of India and Southeast Asia. It is known for its unique, pungent odor and has been traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine for its various health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, which can help to reduce fever, alleviate pain, and promote wound healing. The plant's therapeutic actions include its ability to modulate the immune system, exhibit hepatoprotective effects, and exhibit potential anticancer properties. The bioactive constituents of Sterculia coccinea var. hamiltonii include flavonoids, alkaloids, and saponins, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
